## Finding

For `static char array[64];` the expression `&array + 1` evaluates to `array + 1`. The correct
value is `array + 64`. The ticket's example increments `p` of type `char (*)[64]` with `*p++`,
compares it with `&array + 1`, and gets 0. In the second comment of the ticket the reporter says
that the increment of `p` is correct and that `&array + 1` alone shows the defect. The reporter
used z80. For mcs51 the finding comes from reading the source, which is the same for every port.

## Cause

When `ast2iCode` in `src/SDCCicode.c` generates the code for unary `&`, the array operand is
already a pointer to its first element. `geniCodeAddressOf` returns an iTemp operand of pointer
type unchanged. The result of `&array` therefore has the type pointer to element, and arithmetic
on it is scaled by the element size. The tree node has the correct type, pointer to array, in
`tree->ftype`.

## Fix

For an array operand, `ast2iCode` sets the type of the result of `geniCodeAddressOf` to
`tree->ftype`. The patch attached to the ticket makes the same `setOperandType` call. This patch
makes the call only when the result is an iTemp and `tree->ftype` is a pointer.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-4249.c` has the ticket's example with an array of 16 bytes, and it
asserts `(char *)(&array + 1) == array + 16`. The test in the ticket's patch has more cases.
